title: Claude is picking on me in Discord
author: u3030
selftext: For those of you using Claude Code, adding it to Discord has been amazing.  I can walk away, go outside and then check the status of ongoing work, review art or model generations from my phone, even ask it to play my game on Godot and send screenshots.  Channels capability was added a little while ago and its worth trying out if you haven't already.

comments.author: ziguslav
comments.body: This looks really interesting. What's the setup like? I'm not sure what you mean by the channels capability. Could you expand a bit please?

replies.author: u3030
replies.body: Sure, the setup is pretty straightforward, you're making a discord bot for your channel, pairing it in Claude Code, and you can send/receive messages in Discord that interact with an active Claude Code session.  Here's the channels link, which does a great job explaining how to set it up.  Took me about 30 minutes to get it up and running.  From there you can control your session from Discord just like you would in the terminal: [Push events into a running session with channels - Claude Code Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels)

comments.author: cdgalvan
comments.body: Can you talk more about your setup and how it allows for you to walk away and check on the status of tasks later from your phone? What things are being automated? What tasks is claude making easier for you? What does your setup look like, and what software, if any, are you using in addition to discord and Claude Code and Godot?

replies.author: u3030
replies.body:
Yeah, its using the new Claude Code channels plugin: [Push events into a running session with channels - Claude Code Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels)

  
This allows me to interact with Claude Code via Discord instead of the terminal, so I can go away while Claude works, have it post updates to the channel, send it new tasks, etc.  Just by chatting in Discord.  Its pretty handy. 

  
Lots of things are being automated.  I'm currently working on a game and the primary thing its helping me with is taking my concept art for characters, creating a 3d mesh and texture in Trellis (or Meshy if I need a little more oomph), pulling that mesh into Blender for decimation, auto rigging and animating in ComfyUI.  Then I have Claude render frames from those animations into a sprite sheet using Blender and post to discord for review. 

  
As for tools, Claude Code is pretty central to everything I'm doing for the game, I primarily use it, Blender, and other services like Trellis or Meshy together for the animation pipeline.  It also helps code, debug issues, keep track of bugs/features, etc.
